newsitem.title: USA: Philip Morris paid rival's legal fees - Liggett owner testifies.
newsitem.headline: Philip Morris paid rival's legal fees - Liggett owner testifies.

text.p: Renegade tobacco executive Bennett LeBow testified Monday that industry giant Philip Morris offered to pay his Liggett Group's legal fees to fight anti-tobacco lawsuits during 1995 and that he accepted the money for months.
Lebow told a jury hearing a $5 billion secondhand-smoke case, in which Liggett is one of nine defendants, that the offer came through Liggett's lawyers.
LeBow did not detail how much Philip Morris paid to cover Liggett's legal fees but said his company in 1995 was paying lawyers costs approaching $10 million a year.
"Philip Morris offered to pay all these fees," LeBow said.
LeBow gave few details but said Philip Morris, the richest and most successful of the tobacco companies, stopped paying the fees after a few months.
Liggett is the smallest of the top five U.S. tobacco company and has the shakiest finances, according to industry analysts.
Lawyers defending the tobacco company in the secondhand-smoke case repeatedly interrupted LeBow, who was subpoenaed by lawyers pressing the secondhand-smoke case.
The judge called a recess to allow LeBow to meet with his lawyers after he said he was waving his right to confidentiality in detailing past discussions with his lawyers.

In the past two years LeBow made separate agreements with anti-tobacco forces that were denounced by other cigarette makers but were later seen crucial in bringing about the tentative $368.5 billion settlement announced last month between tobacco companies and state attorneys general suing cigarette makers.
